items.stem: A company created an Auto Scaling group with the AWS CLI and later turned on Elastic Load Balancing health checks for it. The group runs a web application behind an Application Load Balancer. The application needs about 4 minutes after launch before it answers the target group health checks. Now each new instance is terminated and replaced again and again, so the group does not reach its desired capacity. Instances whose application fails later must still be replaced. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
keywords: created an Auto Scaling group with the AWS CLI

options.text: Increase the default cooldown of the group, so that the group waits longer before it replaces an instance that fails its health checks.
options.why: The group [does not wait for the cooldown period](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-cooldown-unhealthy-replacement-does-not-wait) before it replaces an unhealthy instance, so a longer cooldown changes nothing here.
options.misconception: believes that the cooldown delays the replacement of unhealthy instances

options.text: Change the health check type of the group back to Amazon EC2 status checks only, so that the group ignores the target group results.
options.why: It stops the loop, but the group then [only replaces instances that are unhealthy or unreachable](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-lb-default-ec2-checks-only) by the EC2 checks, so a failed application stays.
options.misconception: believes that the EC2 status checks also find a failed application

options.text: Add a launch lifecycle hook, and change the user data script so that it completes the lifecycle action when the application answers requests.
options.why: It works, because with launch hooks you can [set the health check grace period to 0](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-grace-period-zero-with-launch-hooks), but it changes the script and adds a hook to manage.

options.text: Set the health check grace period of the group to a value that is longer than the time that the application needs to start.
options.why: The group runs the ELB checks on a new instance [after a grace period](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-health-optional-checks-after-grace-period), so a period that covers the start ends the loop and keeps the checks.

items.explanation: A group created with the AWS CLI starts with a grace period of [0 seconds](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-grace-period-console-300-cli-0). The ELB checks then start at once, the target group reports each new instance as unhealthy before the application answers, and the group [terminates the unhealthy instance and launches another](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-unhealthy-terminated-replaced). A grace period longer than the 4-minute start breaks the loop and keeps the ELB checks on.
items.takeaway: Set a grace period that covers the application start; with the AWS CLI it starts at [0 seconds](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-grace-period-console-300-cli-0).
items.twin: If the stem said "new instances receive requests before the application is ready" instead: a launch lifecycle hook, because it holds the instance until it is [ready to accept traffic](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-lifecycle-hook-lb-registration).
items.say: A CLI-made group has no grace period, so I'd set one that covers the four-minute start.

solvers.stem_only: A group created with the CLI gets a health check grace period of 0, so ELB health checks fail before the app is ready and the instance is replaced. Set the health check grace period above the ~4 minute startup time; ELB health checks stay on so later failures are still replaced.

keywords: uses only the default Amazon EC2 health checks
the target group marks the instance unhealthy, and the instance still passes its EC2 status checks

options.text: Leave the health check type of the Auto Scaling group as it is, and rely on the group to replace each instance that it finds unhealthy.

options.text: Install an agent on each instance that tests the web server every minute and reports each failed test to the Auto Scaling API as an unhealthy instance.
options.why: It works, because a custom check can [mark that particular instance as](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-custom-health-check-immediate-replace) unhealthy, but the team builds and runs an agent that one setting replaces.

options.text: Configure the Application Load Balancer to replace each target that fails its health checks with a new instance from the launch template of the group.
options.why: A failed check makes the load balancer [stop routing requests to it](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-faq-elb-requests-before-detection-fail); launching a replacement is work for the group.

options.text: Set the health check type of the Auto Scaling group to include Elastic Load Balancing, so that the group acts on the health that the target group reports.
options.why: Then [Elastic Load Balancing stops sending traffic to it](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-elb-checks-reroute-and-replace), and the group [replaces it](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-health-elb-unhealthy-replaced), with one setting and no code to run.

items.explanation: The web server stops while the instance keeps running, so the EC2 status checks still pass. By default the group [ignores the results of the Elastic Load Balancing](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-elb-health-checks-ignored-by-default) health checks. For the ELB health check type, [you must turn it on](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-health-elb-check-must-be-turned-on); then the group marks the instance unhealthy [on its next periodic health check](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-health-elb-unhealthy-replaced) and replaces it.
items.takeaway: A running instance whose web server failed needs the ELB health check type on the group.
items.twin: If the stem said "the underlying hardware of an instance fails, and the instance fails its EC2 system status check" instead: keep the current settings, because EC2 status checks are the [default health check type](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-health-check-type-ec2-default).
items.say: The group ignores the target group's verdict until you turn on ELB health checks, so I'd turn them on.

solvers.stem_only: Turn on Elastic Load Balancing health checks for the Auto Scaling group (health check type ELB), so the group marks instances that fail the target group health check as unhealthy and replaces them automatically; no custom scripts needed.
